\ednentry{
  id = {EDN-79},
  title = {The seller-grouped hash split stays},
  date = {2026-10-12},
  milestone = {M3: Quality Assurance},
  topic = {Evaluation Protocol, Data Splitting},
  participants = {@lukas2510},
  decision = {The split stays as it is: whole sellers assigned by a hash of the seed and the seller key, 60/10/10/20, unstratified, with the committed seed.
The model card states the distribution of every set and gives a figure of the committed split with its spread over 20 other splits.
An adversarial-validation check is recorded once, and the missing temporal split is a stated limitation.},
  rationale = {\emph{Alternatives considered:}
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt]
\item A stratified-group split on \texttt{make}: better make balance, but about half of the existing rows change set when the \texttt{ES} listings join, which confounds FR-15's retrain comparison.
\item Choose a seed for a better mix: a split selected by its outcome.
\item A temporal split: impossible, because the snapshot has no listing dates.
\end{itemize}
\par
\emph{Why:} Over 20 other splits the candidate's test MdAPE is 6.73\,\% on average, with a standard deviation of 0.27 pp, and SC-01 and SC-02 hold on all 20.
Cars older than 20 years exceed the SC-04 bound on all 20 as well, at 18.3\,\% on average, so that miss is no artefact of the draw.
The 20 splits share one pool of listings, so the spread describes how a figure moves with the assignment and is not a confidence interval for new data.},

  response = {Accepted},
  assessment = {AI wrote and ran the evidence script against the stages' own code and first checked that it reproduces the committed metrics.

It laid out the options, recommended this one and stopped for the decision.},
